_doc: Every constant is {value, source}. A run's protocol may override a key via protocol.overrides['section.key']; every override is logged as an amendment. Read values through mgcore.config.get(path).

scouts.source: Smallest number of independent searchers that gives pairwise agreement plus a tie-breaker; matches the deep-research coordinator default of 3 parallel researchers.

overlap_target.source: Design default: vocabulary has a long tail, so the aim is query diversity rather than completeness; stricter targets waste rounds.

max_rounds.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): round 2 added 650 terms but PRESS used ~4% of the 1,325-term union; overlap stayed 0.02-0.05 on a broad topic. One round plus PRESS review gives the query blocks; extra rounds mostly add tail vocabulary.

queries_per_scout.source: Design default: enough query blocks to cover every facet pair at least once per scout.

units_per_scout.source: Research-statistics track: treat each scout x channel family as one sampling unit so T grows fast enough for Chao2 (3 scouts x 3 families = 9 units per round).

completeness_target_theta.source: The user's doctoral-team rule (~90% intersection), enforced as S_obs / Chao2 estimate instead of raw overlap.

coverage_target.source: Chao & Jost 2012 sample coverage; research-statistics track recommendation (stop when C-hat >= 0.95).

max_marginal_yield.source: Wohlin 2014 (stop when an iteration adds ~nothing) and Guest, Namey & Chen 2020 (<=5% new information).

min_units_T.source: Design default: incidence estimators need several sampling units; T>=6 keeps A=(T-1)/T >= 0.83.

min_per_kind.source: Design default: fewer than 3 entities of a kind gives no usable Q1/Q2 split.

max_rounds.source: Budget guard; matches the plan's STOP_UNSATURATED rule.

probe_max_new_share.source: Equals 1 - completeness_target_theta: a fresh holdout searcher should find at most 10% new items if ~90% are already known.

extrapolation_limit_factor.source: Chao & Jost 2012; Chao & Colwell 2017: do not extrapolate beyond double the reference sample size.

z.source: 95% normal quantile used by the log-normal Chao2 interval (Chao & Colwell 2017).

verify_batch.source: Fetches per `entities verify` call at the 3-second politeness interval: about two minutes per call, so a call stays well inside tool timeouts.

min_coverage_gain.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): coverage went 0.11 -> 0.54 -> 0.59 -> 0.68; round 4 cost 3 scouts + 3 screeners for +0.09. Stop (STOP_UNSATURATED) when a round adds less than this much sample coverage (diminishing returns), like the 5% new-information rule of Guest et al. 2020.

max_units_per_scout.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): round 4 gave each scout 12 units for a 20-call budget (<2 searches per unit), so units were sampled too thinly to count. Cap EXPAND at scouts x this value.

max_iterations.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): three iterations added 67, 80 and 82 included entities with no convergence (a broad market keeps branching) and cost 9 scouts + 14 screeners; snowball finds never enter the estimators, and the red team already runs a targeted existence search per gap.

high_yield_flag.source: If snowballing adds more than 1 - theta new verified entities, sampling missed part of the market; flag as a coverage limitation.

audit_fraction.source: O'Connor & Joffe 2020: double-code 10-25% of units; upper-middle value chosen.

audit_min_units.source: Design default: below 10 audited units an agreement coefficient is not informative.

value.EX-NOT-SOFTWARE: Not a software product, community or directory
value.EX-OUT-OF-SCOPE: Outside the protocol scope (segment, job, geography or business model)
value.EX-DEAD: Product discontinued, domain parked or no activity inside the recency window
value.EX-DUPLICATE: Duplicate of another entity under a different key
value.EX-NOT-FOUND: Page does not exist or does not mention the entity
value.EX-EXCLUDED-SOURCE: Only reachable through an excluded source

reason_codes.source: PRISMA 2020 requires reasons for exclusion; codes adapted to software products.

batch_size.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): screeners finished 40-entity batches with spare budget; 60 cuts screener count by a third.

audit_until_units.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): screening alpha was 0.90 over 162 audited entities. Once the cumulative audit has at least this many double-screened units and alpha >= screening.alpha_accept, later batches skip the B audit (saves one subagent per batch); a later revise reopens it.

miners.source: One miner per channel group (marketplaces/vendor pages, communities/Q&A, signals/why-now).

quote_max_chars.source: Data minimisation (GDPR art. 5(1)(c)); data-sources track recommendation of <=280-char quotes.

retention_days.source: Design default retention limit for snapshots containing personal data; GDPR storage-limitation principle.

min_interval_seconds.source: Polite per-domain spacing for pages without a documented API limit.

robots_cache_hours.source: RFC 9309 section 2.4: crawlers should not use a cached robots.txt for more than 24 hours.

stoptest_pool_min.source: Design default: below ~200 candidates screen everything; the statistical stop only pays off on large ranked pools.

strength_weights.source: Ordinal weights on the Mom Test / Testing Business Ideas evidence ladder (facts over opinions, doing over saying); tunable design default.

stale_months.source: Data-sources track: flag evidence older than 12 months.

max_targeted_rounds.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): after round 1, 11 of 12 cards failed mainly on source diversity (<3 domains); one targeted round on near-miss cards from new domains lifted passing cards from 1 to 3. Cap the automatic targeted rounds per run.

target_candidates.source: Design default: if fewer than this many cards pass `cards check` and near-misses fail only on fixable evidence counts, run a targeted evidence round.

max_domain_share.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): round 1 drew 158 of 165 records from two sites (news.ycombinator.com, itunes.apple.com). Above this share for the top two domains, miners are told which domains to avoid and the dossier flags concentration.

open_base_n.source: Design default: enough short records to draft a codebook of 20-40 codes (O'Connor & Joffe 2020 suggest keeping codebooks to roughly 20-40 codes).

reliability_min_units.source: Design default: smaller samples make per-code alpha unstable.

min_positives_per_code.source: O'Connor & Joffe 2020: rare codes depress kappa/alpha; require a minimum number of positives before judging a code.

max_revisions.source: Budget guard; after three revisions remaining weak codes are carried as provisional and downgrade certainty.

theme_coverage_target.source: Research-statistics track: treat records x themes as incidence data and require C-hat >= 0.95.

gnc_base.source: Adaptation of Guest, Namey & Chen 2020 (base 4 for interviews) to short desk posts; documented as an adaptation.

gnc_run.source: Adaptation of Guest, Namey & Chen 2020 (run 2-3 for interviews) to short desk posts.

value.label: Fragmentation
value.definition: The person juggles several tools or places to get one job done; there is no single place.
value.include: Mentions switching between tools, copying data between apps, or many tools for one job.
value.exclude: A single tool lacking one feature (use a pain or feature code).

value.label: Integration missing
value.definition: Tools the person uses do not connect or sync with each other.
value.include: No integration, broken sync, manual export/import between named tools.
value.exclude: General complaints about a tool's own features.

value.label: Price mismatch
value.definition: Too expensive for the value received or for this segment.
value.include: Explicit cost complaints, seat pricing that does not fit, no small tier.
value.exclude: Statements about willingness to pay without complaint (use stance wtp).

value.label: Too complex
value.definition: The product is too complex or heavy for this user or use case.
value.include: Bloat, steep learning curve, built for bigger teams.

value.label: Language or locale missing
value.definition: Language, currency, tax, date format or local compliance is not supported.
value.include: Translation gaps, missing local currency or tax rules, regional regulation.

value.label: Support gap
value.definition: Support is missing, slow or unhelpful.
value.include: Unanswered tickets, no human support, slow responses.

value.label: Reliability
value.definition: The product breaks, loses data or is unavailable.
value.include: Bugs, data loss, outages, failed syncs.

value.label: Pain grows with volume
value.definition: The pain grows as usage, volume, clients or team size grow (dose-response).
value.include: 'Fine at 5 clients, impossible at 50', costs scaling with volume.
value.exclude: Pain that is constant regardless of volume.

value.label: Push of the situation
value.definition: Something in the current situation pushes the person to seek change.
value.include: Frustration events, deadlines missed, a breaking point.
value.exclude: Attraction to a specific new product (use F-PULL).

value.label: Pull of the new solution
value.definition: An attraction to a new way of doing the job.
value.include: 'I saw X does Y and wanted that', promised outcomes.
value.exclude: Complaints about the old way (use F-PUSH).

value.label: Anxiety of the new
value.definition: Worries that hold back switching to a new solution.
value.include: Migration risk, learning cost, fear it will not work.
value.exclude: Satisfaction with the current tool (use F-HABIT).

value.label: Habit of the present
value.definition: Comfort with the current way that holds back switching.
value.include: 'Good enough', 'we have always used', sunk cost.
value.exclude: Fears about the new tool (use F-ANX).

value.label: First thought
value.definition: The moment the person first realised the current way is not good enough.

value.label: Active looking
value.definition: Actively searching, comparing and trialling options.
value.include: Trials, comparisons, demo requests, 'looking for an alternative'.

value.label: Deciding
value.definition: Choosing and committing, including what tipped the decision.

value.label: Consuming
value.definition: Experience after switching: onboarding, first value, regret or delight.

standard_codes.source: Cross-cutting pains from the market-gap taxonomy; Forces of Progress and switch timeline from Moesta & Spiek (jobstobedone.org); added by `codebook freeze` so every run uses the same definitions (method card D13).

theme_code_types.source: Method card D14: theme saturation counts the run's own codes; standard X-/F-/T- codes exist by construction and are left out.

batch_size.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): coders finished 60-100 record batches in ~2-3 minutes with spare budget; amendment 6 used 100 without quality loss (alpha 0.85 on strength).

max_own_codes.source: Design default, not an empirical threshold: the run's own codes that one coder can apply consistently from a single context. Standard X-/F-/T- codes, sharpened or not, do not count; the live run's v2 codebook had 36 own codes.

absolute_supply_max.source: Evidence Gap Map convention: an absolute gap is a cell with few or no primary studies; here <=1 product serving the job.

synthesis_supply_min.source: Design default: 5+ point solutions for one job indicates a fragmented, rebundling-prone cell (EGM 'synthesis gap' analogue).

synthesis_fragmentation_share.source: Design default: at least 20% of the job's demand evidence complains about fragmentation or integration.

min_demand_authors.source: Matches gap_card.min_records; marketingskills/customer-research prior art uses >=5 data points per segment.

assoc_min_cooccurrence.source: Design default: association strength is unstable for co-occurrence counts below 3.

min_records.source: Prior art (customer-research skill) requires >=5 data points; plan threshold.

min_domains.source: Triangulation across independent sources (data-sources track lesson 4).

min_source_types.source: Methodological triangulation (Denzin): at least two kinds of source.

min_authors.source: A single author is an anecdote, not a pattern.

require_triangulation.source: Data-sources track: combine pain + demand + supply before calling something a gap.

bias_moderate.source: Design operationalisation of GRADE risk-of-bias for market evidence (share of vendor/incentivized/affiliate sources).

inconsistency_moderate.source: Design operationalisation of GRADE inconsistency (contra / (support + contra)).

indirect_moderate.source: Design operationalisation of GRADE indirectness (share of stated-not-revealed or adjacent-persona evidence).

authors_serious_below.source: CERQual adequacy: too few independent authors.

ci_width_moderate.source: GRADE imprecision: a wide Wilson interval on a prevalence proportion.

coverage_moderate_below.source: Publication-bias analogue: low landscape coverage means unseen supply.

magnitude_min_authors.source: GRADE large-effect upgrade analogue: money spent on workarounds by >=3 authors.

dose_response_min_authors.source: GRADE dose-response upgrade analogue: pain that grows with usage (X-SCALE) from >=3 authors.

weights.source: Design default emphasising Pain and Pay because 'no market need' is consistently a top startup failure reason (CB Insights post-mortems); override in the protocol.

dirichlet_concentration.source: Design default: weights vary by roughly +/-30% relative around the defaults.

draws.source: Monte Carlo draws for p_top3; standard error < 0.012 for any probability.

top_n.source: Report the probability of landing in the top 3.

gates.source: Plan: hard gates before scores (regulatory load, human-ops burden, agent-buildability, platform risk, ToS feasibility).

top_products.source: Budget guard on the morphological box (Zwicky): vary only the strongest proven products.

s.source: Kleinberg 2002 two-state model; research-statistics track recommends s=2 for short series.

shuffles.source: Permutation test with 200 timestamp shuffles (p resolution 0.005).

alpha.source: Conventional significance level for the shuffle test.

gap_match_jaccard.source: Plan: two gaps match when their incumbents + evidence URLs overlap with Jaccard >= 0.3.

rbo_p.source: Webber, Moffat & Zobel 2010: p=0.9 weights roughly the top 10 ranks.

subagents_max.source: Cost guard; next refuses to plan another spawn once spent.

scout_tool_calls.source: Plan: cap each scout at ~15-20 tool calls.

miner_tool_calls.source: Miners read more pages per item than scouts.

models._doc: Model tier per subagent role. Scripts verify quotes, schemas, agreement and screening, so cheap tiers are safe for roles whose output is machine-checked; judgment-heavy roles get stronger tiers. A failed check escalates that role one tier for its next assignment.

profile.source: Design default; the protocol may set cost_profile to budget, balanced or quality.

profiles.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): ~91 assignments, of which ~75 (scouts, screeners, miners, coders) produce output that scripts verify (100% of 289 quotes verified, screening alpha 0.90, coding alpha >= 0.80 after revision). Those roles can run on the fast tier; synthesis, red team and writing need judgment.

harness_names.source: Claude Code Agent tool model parameter accepts haiku/sonnet/opus; OpenCode uses provider/model ids; Codex model names change, so they are left to the operator.

escalate_on.source: Same thresholds the method already uses (D09 >= 95% quotes verified, D06/D14 alpha bands); a failed check bumps the role one tier.

broad_jobs_warning.source: Live run indie-dev-tools (2026-10-09): an intervention naming 7 jobs gave lexicon overlap 0.02-0.05, a 395-entity landscape that never saturated and evidence too thin for 11 of 12 gap cards. protocol check warns at this many jobs (non-blocking).
